summary: 165-line, comment-dominated sketch inside `Module PrototypeTheory` with no Theorem/Lemma/Example and no proof; its only machine-checked content is three `Eval compute` calls (0, 2, 2). It flattens Lakoff 1987's cluster model for 'mother' (birth, genetic, nurturance, marital, genealogical models) into a five-Boolean Record (genealogical model dropped, `female` added from the central-case description), fixes an all-true CentralMother, defines a Hamming distance and a context-weighted Hamming distance from it, and defines membership as 'weighted distance below a nat threshold'. This is the weighted-feature-bundle / linear-representativeness model that Lakoff 1987 explicitly rejects (ch. 5 'mere shadows of cognitive models'; ch. 7 'weighted feature bundles simply don't come close'), and the file's premise that Lakoff's categories have graded membership to be modelled in [0,1] is the reading Lakoff 1987 ch. 2 calls 'a mistaken interpretation of the data', citing his own 1972/1973 'Hedges' as the typical example. The header's 'Key Concept', radial categories, is never defined; metonymic stereotypes, the gestalt property of clusters and the 1973 fuzzy-logic-with-hedges apparatus are absent. The closing claim (L150-162) that the encoding 'lost' universal quantification, modus ponens and compositionality is refuted by the file's own code: membership is a decidable nat inequality over which quantified, decidability and monotonicity lemmas close under the global context (scratch-verified). Real-valued Degree/measure/Category are dead code; weighted_distance silently ignores `female`. Compiles; 0 theorems; 0 propositional axioms; verdict unfaithful; determination major_restructuring (agreeing with the survey, on different grounds from the file's).

sources.citation: Lakoff, G. (1987). Women, Fire, and Dangerous Things: What Categories Reveal about the Mind. University of Chicago Press. Passages read (PDF page indices of the on-disk 752-page file): ch. 2 'From Wittgenstein to Rosch' (Zadeh, p. 39; Rosch ratings retraction, p. 67; summary, p. 81); ch. 4 'Idealized Cognitive Models' ('Cluster Models', 'Mother', pp. 103-104; bachelor/ICM fit, p. 98); ch. 5 'Metonymic Models' ('Working Mothers', pp. 109-111; composite prototype and representativeness structures, p. 112; 'Radial Structures', pp. 112-114); ch. 6 'Radial Categories' (p. 123); ch. 7 'Features, Stereotypes, and Defaults' ('Feature Bundles', p. 152); ch. 9 'Defenders of the Classical View' (Osherson & Smith, pp. 182-183; summary, pp. 198-199); ch. 13 'What's Wrong with Objectivist Cognition' ('ICM Clusterings', p. 260; 'Radial Structures', p. 262); ch. 17 'Cognitive Semantics' (Spatialization of Form, p. 360; 'Feature-Bundle Structures', 'Radial Category Structure', 'Graded Categories', 'Prototypes', pp. 364-367).

Lakoff, G. (1973). Hedges: A Study in Meaning Criteria and the Logic of Fuzzy Concepts. Journal of Philosophical Logic 2(4): 458-508 (revised from CLS 8, 1972; the 1987 book's bibliography and its p. 67 cite it as 'Lakoff 1972'). Sections read: 1 'Degrees of Truth' (birdiness hierarchy (1), degree-of-truth (4), pp. 459-461); 2 'Fuzzy Logic' (Zadeh definition (1) with max/min/1-x, p. 461; degree of entailment, p. 470); 3 'Hedges' (hedge list incl. 'a real', p. 472; technically/strictly speaking/loosely speaking/regular, pp. 475-477; criterion types (16) and informal hedge semantics (17), pp. 477-478); 4 'Fuzzy Logic with Hedges' (vector value ||F||, def/prim/sec/char, hedge valuations (3), pp. 478-479). Not cited by the Coq file, which names only the 1987 book.

definitions_mapped.coq: Parameter Degree : Type; Parameter measure : Degree -> R (L31-32)
definitions_mapped.source: Zadeh membership value mu_A(x) 'in the real interval [0,1], though the values can also be taken to be members of any distributive complemented lattice' (1973 sec. 2 def. (1), p. 461); 'Graded Categories' scale between 0 and 1 (1987 ch. 17, PDF p. 365)
definitions_mapped.note: No [0,1] constraint on the image of `measure`. Both declarations are dead code: grep shows Degree and measure occur only at L31-32. Coq.Reals is imported solely for them and for Category.

definitions_mapped.coq: Parameter Entity : Type; Definition Category := Entity -> R (L34-37)
definitions_mapped.source: fuzzy set A = {(x, mu_A(x))} on a universe of discourse X (1973 (1), p. 461); graded category (1987 ch. 17, PDF p. 365)
definitions_mapped.note: Signature only: no bound on values (`fun _ : Entity => (42 * PI)%R : Category` typechecks, scratch-verified) and none of the 1973 (1) operations (union = max, intersection = min, complement = 1 - mu, subset) is defined. Never used; every category in the file is a MotherFeatures record with nat-valued distances instead.

definitions_mapped.coq: Record MotherFeatures {gives_birth, gives_genes, provides_nurtur, married_father, female : bool} (L46-52)
definitions_mapped.source: cluster model for mother: birth model, genetic model, nurturance model, marital model, genealogical model (1987 ch. 4 'Mother', PDF p. 103); central-case description 'is and always has been female, ... gave birth, supplied her half of the child's genes, nurtured the child, is married to the father, is one generation older than the child, and is the child's legal guardian' (ch. 5 'Radial Structures', PDF p. 112)
definitions_mapped.note: A cluster of five cognitive models, each an ICM with its own internal structure, becomes an unstructured bundle of five independent Booleans, which is exactly what ch. 7 (PDF p. 152) defines as a 'feature bundle' and what ch. 13 (PDF p. 260) calls 'conceptual atomism (sometimes known as feature semantics)', the doctrine the cluster's gestalt property is said to contradict. The genealogical model, the generation condition and legal guardianship are dropped; `female` is taken from the central-case description, not from the cluster. L40 labels this a '(Lakoff 1987, Case Study)'; it is in Book I ch. 4-6, not among the book's three Case Studies (anger, over, there-constructions).

definitions_mapped.source: 'The central case, where all the models converge' (ch. 5, PDF p. 112); 'the ideal case, where the models converge' (ch. 4, PDF p. 104)
definitions_mapped.note: Adequate for the four models it keeps; the center is the all-true vector.

definitions_mapped.coq: feature_distance : Hamming distance on the five Booleans (L64-69)
definitions_mapped.source: no source definition. Nearest text: 'the closer an individual is to the prototype, the more representative a mother she is. Representativeness structures are linear. They concern nothing but closeness to the prototypical case, and thus they hide most of the richness of structure ... mere shadows of cognitive models' (ch. 5, PDF p. 112)
definitions_mapped.note: The source names linear closeness-to-prototype only to deny that it is the category's structure and defines no metric. The file makes this metric the structure of the category, in place of the radial structure of ch. 6 whose extensions are 'not generated from the central model by general rules' (PDF p. 123). A metric grades all 32 feature vectors, whereas ch. 5 (PDF p. 113) insists 'not all possible variations on the central case exist as categories'.

definitions_mapped.coq: StepmotherFeatures := {birth f; genes f; nurtur t; married t; female t} (L72-78)
definitions_mapped.source: 'Stepmother: She didn't give birth or supply the genes, but she is currently married to the father' (ch. 5, PDF p. 112)
definitions_mapped.note: provides_nurtur := true is the file's addition; the source characterization mentions only birth, genes and marriage (nurturance is what distinguishes adoptive and foster mothers on the same page).

definitions_mapped.coq: BirthMotherFeatures := {birth t; genes t; nurtur f; married f; female t} (L80-86)
definitions_mapped.source: 'Birth mother: This is defined in contrast to adoptive mother; given an adoption ICM, the woman who gives birth and puts the child up for adoption' (ch. 5, PDF p. 112); the unwed mother who gives up her child (ch. 5, PDF p. 110)
definitions_mapped.note: married_father := false and gives_genes := true are the file's inferences (the source reserves unmarried status for 'unwed mother'); the adoption ICM relative to which the source says the term is defined has no counterpart.

Worked computations only. They rank stepmother and birth mother as equally distant from the center; the source never ranks them and says a full study 'must go well beyond just isolating a prototype and giving a linear ranking of how close nonprototypical cases are' (ch. 5, PDF p. 112).

definitions_mapped.coq: Record ContextWeights {w_birth, w_genes, w_nurtur, w_marriage : nat}; BiologicalContext := {10,10,1,0}; SocialContext := {1,0,10,5} (L117-128)
definitions_mapped.source: 'real mother' sentences showing that more than one model can ground 'real', and that 'the very idea that there is such a thing as a real mother seems to require a choice among models where they diverge' (ch. 4, PDF p. 103); 'a real' listed among hedges (1973 p. 472) but not analysed; criterion types definitional/primary/secondary/characteristic (1973 (16)-(17), pp. 477-478) and def/prim/sec/char selecting components of the vector value ||F|| combined by fuzzy intersection (1973 (3), p. 479)
definitions_mapped.note: Numeric per-feature weights appear in neither source. The 1987 text says 'real' forces a choice of one model, not a reweighting; the 1973 apparatus selects criterion types and combines by min, not by weighted sum. Weighted feature bundles are precisely the Coleman-Kay-style device that ch. 7 (PDF p. 152) says 'simply do not provide enough structure' and 'cannot account for radial structures'.

definitions_mapped.source: 'A weighted feature bundle assigns weights to the features in a bundle ... Deviation from the prototype in highly weighted features places a member further away from the prototype than deviation in a less highly weighted feature' (ch. 7 'Feature Bundles', PDF p. 152), presented there as a failed early theory
definitions_mapped.note: The file implements, as Lakoff's model, the model Lakoff describes in order to reject it. Internally inconsistent with feature_distance: ContextWeights has no w_female, so `female` is ignored. Scratch: a vector with birth f, genes f, nurtur t, married t, female f has feature_distance 3 but weighted_distance 1 under SocialContext, and `female_ignored : forall w f, weighted_distance w CentralMother f = weighted_distance w CentralMother (f with female := negb f.(female))` is proved by `destruct f; reflexivity`.

definitions_mapped.coq: is_category_member ctx thr f := weighted_distance ctx CentralMother f < thr (L143-144)
definitions_mapped.source: closest analogue: 'threshold value for simple category membership' in the informal hedge account (1973 (17), p. 477). In 1987, membership in the radial category is by conventional extension from the center (ch. 6, PDF p. 123; ch. 13, PDF p. 262), not by threshold; 'not all possible variations on the central case exist as categories' (ch. 5, PDF p. 113)
definitions_mapped.note: An ordinary Prop over nat. Scratch (importing the compiled .vo): `member_dec : forall w t f, {is_category_member w t f} + {~ is_category_member w t f}` via lt_dec; `threshold_mono : forall w t1 t2 f, t1 <= t2 -> is_category_member w t1 f -> is_category_member w t2 f`; `step_is_social_mother : is_category_member SocialContext 5 StepmotherFeatures` (weighted distance 1) and `step_not_bio_mother : ~ is_category_member BiologicalContext 5 StepmotherFeatures` (weighted distance 20); all Qed, Print Assumptions 'Closed under the global context'. This contradicts the file's own comments at L137-141 and L150-162.

definitions_mapped.source: radial category: 'a central case and conventionalized variations on it which cannot be predicted by general rules' (ch. 5, PDF p. 114); extensions 'not generated from the central model by general rules; instead, they are extended by convention and must be learned one by one', motivated by 'general principles of extension' (ch. 6, PDF p. 123); three components — conventional choice of center, extension principles (metaphoric, metonymic, image-schematic), specific conventional extensions (ch. 13, PDF p. 262); CENTER-PERIPHERY schema (ch. 17, PDF pp. 360, 365)
definitions_mapped.note: The construct the header (L4) names as the file's key concept is not defined anywhere in the file, and its defining property (no general rule generates the extensions) is negated by the file's rule (threshold on a metric).

definitions_mapped.source: metonymic model: the housewife-mother stereotype standing for the whole category; 'working mother' defined against it relative to the nurturance model alone, so a birth mother who gave her child up and works 'is not a working mother' (ch. 5, PDF pp. 109-110); composite prototype (PDF pp. 111-112)
definitions_mapped.note: The source's second source of prototype effects for mother; absent.

definitions_mapped.source: gestalt property of the cluster: 'mother is an easier concept to comprehend than ... birth mother, genetic mother, legal mother', inconsistent with 'conceptual atomism (sometimes known as feature semantics)' (ch. 13 'ICM Clusterings', PDF p. 260)
definitions_mapped.note: The file's feature bundle is the atomist representation the source says cannot capture this.

definitions_mapped.source: 1973 sec. 2 (1) fuzzy union/intersection/complement/subset (p. 461); sec. 4: vector value ||F|| = (mu_G1, ..., mu_Gk) (2)-(3), functions def/prim/sec/char, hedge valuations TECH/STR/LOOS/REG (3) (pp. 478-479); criterion types (16) and informal semantics (17) (pp. 477-478)
definitions_mapped.note: The only explicitly formal apparatus in either source is entirely absent, although the file's L109-114 gestures at exactly the phenomenon (the hedge 'real' shifting which criteria count) that this apparatus was built for. Lakoff's own verdict on (17) is that it 'cannot be handled within the framework of fuzzy logic as developed above' nor 'by any logic developed to date' (p. 478).

definitions_mapped.source: ch. 2 (PDF p. 67): reading Rosch's goodness-of-example ratings as graded bird membership 'was a mistaken interpretation of the data. (See Lakoff 1972 for a typical example.)'; bird 'has strict boundaries and ... robins, owls, and penguins are all 100 percent members'; ch. 9 (PDF pp. 182-183): rejection of the EFFECTS = STRUCTURE and PROTOTYPE = REPRESENTATION interpretations ('membership ... graded, determined by similarity to the concept's best exemplar'); ch. 2 summary (PDF p. 81): 'Other categories, like bird, have clear boundaries; but within those boundaries there are graded prototype effects'
definitions_mapped.note: The file's L19-24 asserts precisely the reading the source retracts, and attributes it to 'Lakoff's Cognitive Semantics'.

evidence: Compiles under Coq 8.20.1 with exit 0; the only output is the three `Eval compute` results 0, 2, 2 (L95-101). The file contains no Theorem/Lemma/Corollary/Proposition/Fact/Example and no proof, so no source claim is verified.

Premise contradicts the primary source. L19-26: 'In Lakoff's Cognitive Semantics, membership is graded. A Robin is a better bird than a Penguin ... we need a degree of membership [0,1]'. Lakoff 1987 ch. 2 (PDF p. 67) says that reading Rosch's ratings as graded bird membership 'was a mistaken interpretation of the data', cites 'Lakoff 1972' (= the Hedges paper on disk, per the bibliography) as 'a typical example', and holds that bird 'has strict boundaries'; the ch. 2 summary (PDF p. 81) separates graded categories (tall man, red) from clear-boundary categories with prototype effects (bird); ch. 9 (PDF pp. 182-183) rejects the EFFECTS = STRUCTURE and PROTOTYPE = REPRESENTATION interpretations. Mother is treated throughout as a clear-boundary category with cluster/radial structure (a stepmother or adoptive mother is a mother), never as a fuzzy set.

Core construct is one the source rejects by name. L131-144 encode a weighted feature bundle with distance-from-prototype and threshold membership; L140 attributes 'weighted_distance(Prototype, X, Context) < Threshold' to 'Lakoff'. Ch. 7 'Feature Bundles' (PDF p. 152) defines exactly this device ('deviation from the prototype in highly weighted features places a member further away') as an early failed approach and concludes 'weighted feature bundles simply don't come close to being able to account for the full range of prototype effects', specifically that they 'cannot account for radial structures' and 'cannot describe motivated, conventional extensions that have to be learned one by one'. Ch. 5 (PDF p. 112) calls linear closeness-to-prototype a 'representativeness structure' that is a 'mere shadow' of the cognitive models.

The defining property of radial categories is negated rather than encoded. Ch. 5 (PDF pp. 113-114) and ch. 6 (PDF p. 123): the subcategories 'are not generated from the central model by general rules' and 'not all possible variations on the central case exist as categories'. The file's is_category_member is a general rule, and its metric grades every one of the 32 feature vectors. Nothing in the file corresponds to the three components of radial structuring listed in ch. 13 (PDF p. 262).

The cluster of five cognitive models (ch. 4, PDF p. 103) becomes five Booleans (L46-52), dropping the genealogical model, the generation condition and legal guardianship (PDF p. 112). Ch. 13 'ICM Clusterings' (PDF p. 260) argues the cluster's gestalt property is 'inconsistent with the doctrine of conceptual atomism (sometimes known as feature semantics)'; the file adopts feature semantics.

The 'context' device (L109-128) has no source counterpart. Ch. 4 (PDF p. 103) says 'real mother' 'seems to require a choice among models where they diverge', i.e. selection of one model, not numeric reweighting; the 1973 hedge apparatus ((16)-(17) pp. 477-478; (3) p. 479) selects criterion types and combines them by fuzzy intersection (min), not by weighted sums, and 'a real' is listed (p. 472) but not analysed.

Self-refuting conclusion. L150-162 claims the encoding 'lost' universal quantification, modus ponens and compositionality and that Category C papers 'require a probabilistic or fuzzy logic'. A scratch module importing the compiled LakoffPrototypes.vo proves member_dec (decidability via lt_dec), threshold_mono (a universally quantified monotonicity law), step_is_social_mother and step_not_bio_mother, all Qed with Print Assumptions 'Closed under the global context'. Quantification and inference over the file's membership predicate behave exactly as in classical logic. Lakoff himself says graded categorization 'is consistent with most of the objectivist assumptions' (ch. 9, PDF p. 183) and that what is 'inexpressible' is radial structuring (ch. 13, PDF p. 262), which the file does not model. The file's fuzzy-logic remedy is also disowned by the 1973 source for the hedge facts (17): 'cannot be handled within the framework of fuzzy logic' (p. 478).

Internal inconsistency: weighted_distance (L131-135) ignores `female` while feature_distance (L64-69) counts it; scratch shows a male stepmother-vector has feature_distance 3 but weighted_distance 1 under SocialContext, and `female_ignored` is provable by `destruct f; reflexivity`.

Dead declarations: Degree, measure, Category (L31-37) and the Reals import are never used; all arithmetic is on nat. The stated need for a real-valued [0,1] domain (L25-26) is not acted on and is not forced by the source either, since 1973 (1) allows membership values in 'any distributive complemented lattice'.

Minor source-labelling errors: L40 calls the mother analysis a 'Case Study' (it is Book I ch. 4-6, not one of the three Case Studies); StepmotherFeatures adds nurturance and BirthMotherFeatures adds unmarried status beyond the source's characterizations (PDF p. 112).
omissions: Radial category structure: conventional center plus conventional, non-rule-generated extensions with extension principles (1987 ch. 5 pp. 112-114; ch. 6 p. 123; ch. 13 p. 262; ch. 17 p. 365).
Genealogical model, generation condition and legal-guardian condition of the mother cluster (ch. 4 p. 103; ch. 5 p. 112).
Metonymic models: housewife-mother stereotype, the working-mother contrast defined relative to the nurturance model, composite prototype (ch. 5 pp. 109-112).
Gestalt property of clusters / anti-atomism argument (ch. 13 'ICM Clusterings' p. 260).

Zadeh operations union/intersection/complement/subset (1973 (1) p. 461) and the fuzzy-logic-with-hedges apparatus: vector values, def/prim/sec/char, hedge valuations (1973 (16), (17), (3), pp. 477-479).
The ch. 2 retraction of graded bird membership (p. 67) and the ch. 9 argument against similarity-to-prototype membership (pp. 182-183), both of which bear directly on the file's premise.
Any theorem, lemma or example verifying a source claim.
additions: Hamming distance feature_distance (L64-69) and weighted Hamming distance weighted_distance (L131-135): a metric the source neither defines nor endorses, and a weighted feature bundle the source explicitly rejects (ch. 7 p. 152).
Threshold membership is_category_member (L143-144), a general rule for category membership that ch. 6 says does not exist.
provides_nurtur := true for stepmother and married_father := false for birth mother (L72-86), beyond the source's characterizations.
The attribution of graded membership and of the weighted-distance-threshold model to Lakoff (L22-24, L140).
simplifications: Five cognitive models flattened to five Booleans; central case as the all-true vector (L46-61).
Membership scale nat instead of [0,1] (L118-121, L143-144).

determination_rationale: The survey entry for this source (papers.json id 121, category C) predicts major_restructuring, and that is what the source reading supports, though this file evidences it weakly because it formalizes a model the source disowns and proves nothing. The precisely specified parts of the theory encode without artifacts: the mother cluster (ch. 4) as five predicates or ICMs; the enumerated conventional subcategories (ch. 5, PDF p. 112) as a finite list; the skeleton of a radial category (center plus a finite graph of labelled extension links, ch. 13 p. 262, ch. 17 p. 365); Zadeh fuzzy sets and the criterion-type vector of Lakoff 1973 secs. 2 and 4 as membership functions into R, Q or any distributive complemented lattice (1973 (1)) with min/max/1-x. What carries the theory's explanatory weight is not specified anywhere in either source: the extension principles (metaphoric, metonymic, image-schematic models), 'motivation', the notion of an ICM 'fitting' a situation (ch. 4 p. 98), the gestalt claim that a whole cluster is cognitively simpler than its parts (ch. 13 p. 260), and Lakoff's own admission that 'there is no theory of which kinds of best examples take precedence' (ch. 17 p. 367). Any Coq rendering must invent these, which is the rubric's 'replacing an informally specified operation by an explicit algorithm the source does not give'. This file's invention, a weighted Hamming metric plus threshold, is the linear representativeness structure that ch. 5 dismisses and the weighted feature bundle that ch. 7 rejects, so it is not a faithful formalization even of the specified part; its core definitions are `changed`. 'cannot' is not evidenced: the file's stated obstruction (L25-26, 'Coq's Prop is binary') is not a foundational conflict, since graded membership is a total function into an ordered domain, exactly Zadeh's definition, and Lakoff himself says graded categorization is consistent with most objectivist assumptions (ch. 9 p. 183); the genuine resistance is underspecification of ICMs and extension principles, which the file neither identifies nor documents, and the rubric requires a diagnosed point of underspecification for 'cannot'. 'as_is' and 'slight_modification' are excluded because no faithful formalization exists and none of the source's headline claims (extensions are conventional and not rule-generated; cluster/radial/metonymic structure is inexpressible in objectivist terms; hedges need typed criteria beyond fuzzy logic) is stated, let alone proved. The file's claim that quantification, modus ponens and compositionality are lost (L150-162) is refuted by its own code.

source_gap: None. Both primary sources are on disk in full with usable text layers: the 1987 book (752-page PDF; chapters 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 13 and 17 extracted with pdftotext and read) and the 1973 Journal of Philosophical Logic paper (eScholarship scan of pp. 458-508 with some letter-spacing noise in the OCR but fully legible; secs. 1-4 read). The book's p. 67 and bibliography cite the paper as 'Lakoff 1972' (CLS 8 version); the 1973 JPL reprint on disk is the standard version and contains the cited passages. The Coq file itself cites only the 1987 book.
